design_understanding: Stage 1 (layman to article/section): the user speaks in layman words — e.g. 'my husband is not giving me money', 'he took my gold', 'they are throwing me out' — and Laya must first convert each such phrase into legal terms (maintenance / neglect to maintain, Stridhan / return of property, right to reside in the shared household, custody, domestic violence, divorce) and then, via a Laya choice question per phrase, map those legal terms to candidate sections from the verified list only. Stage 2 (recheck inside the article section): after Stage 1 picks sections, each picked section is rechecked against ALL of its relations inside that section — its prerequisites, its exclusions/not_for list, its related/co-firing sections, its guardrails and its court — and only sections that survive that recheck stay in the final answer. A section that fails recheck (for example HMA 24 with no HMA proceeding pending, HMA 13/13B when divorce was not asked for, Rajnesh v. Neha cited for Stridhan, Satish Chander Ahuja cited for custody, or residence labelled 'tenancy rights') must be DROPPED with a reason, not kept. Example rechecks built into this phrasebook: maintenance phrases recheck BNSS 144 against HMA 24 vs 25 and PWDVA 20 without double-counting; Stridhan phrases recheck HMA 27 together with BNS 316; custody phrases recheck the welfare-of-the-child principle overriding the HMGA s.6 natural-guardian default; residence phrases recheck PWDVA 17+18+19+20 as a set.
